cards.description: Runs a command with its arguments on the Darwin machine, optionally in a specified working directory.

cwd.description: Current working directory, leave empty in most cases

cards.name: run_command
usage_rules: Provide the command and its arguments as a single string in the required command field.
Set cwd to choose a working directory; otherwise leave it empty.

cards.description: Runs a script on the Darwin machine by piping the script to an interpreter's standard input.

cwd.description: Current working directory, leave empty in most cases

interpreter.description: Command with arguments. Script will be piped to stdin. Examples: bash, fish, zsh, python, or: bash --norc

cards.name: run_script
usage_rules: Provide the script in the required script field.
Optionally specify interpreter as a command with arguments, such as bash or python.
Set cwd to choose a working directory; otherwise leave it empty.

cards.description: 获取指定时区的详细时间信息，包括年、月、日、时、分、秒等；可选择 12 小时制、星期显示区域设置，以及是否包含毫秒级时间戳。

hour12.description: 是否使用 12 小时制格式化时区时间。默认为 false

includeTimestamp.description: 是否在结果中包含毫秒级时间戳。默认为 false

locale.description: 用于本地化星期显示的区域设置。默认为 zh-CN

timezone.description: 时区（例如：Asia/Shanghai, UTC）。默认为系统时区

cards.name: get_time_info
usage_rules: 可选提供 timezone（如 Asia/Shanghai 或 UTC）；未提供时使用系统时区。
可选提供 hour12，控制时区时间是否采用 12 小时制；默认 false。
可选提供 locale，用于本地化星期显示；默认 zh-CN。
可选提供 includeTimestamp，控制结果是否包含毫秒级时间戳；默认 false。

cards.description: 获取当前日期和时间，可指定时区及返回格式。

format.description: 时间格式：'iso'（ISO 8601）、'locale'（本地格式）、'timestamp'（时间戳）。默认为 'iso'

timezone.description: 时区（例如：Asia/Shanghai, UTC, America/New_York）。默认为系统时区

cards.name: get_current_time
usage_rules: 可选提供 format：iso 表示 ISO 8601，locale 表示本地格式，timestamp 表示时间戳；默认 iso。
format 仅接受 iso、locale 或 timestamp。
可选提供 timezone（如 Asia/Shanghai、UTC 或 America/New_York）；未提供时使用系统时区。

cards.description: Executes a custom sequence of MCP tool calls. Each step identifies the MCP server and tool to invoke, can include tool parameters, and may declare dependencies on other named steps.
cards.name: run_sequence
usage_rules: Provide the required steps array; each step must include name, mcp, and tool.
Use name values to identify steps and dependsOn to list step names that a step depends on.
Include params as an object containing the called tool's parameters when needed.
Use this tool when you need to specify the tool-call sequence and dependencies directly.

cards.description: Lists the available pre-built workflows and their descriptions.
cards.name: list_workflows
usage_rules: Call with no arguments; this tool accepts an empty input object.
Use it to discover available pre-built workflows before selecting one to run.

cards.description: Runs an intelligent workflow, using an optional focus area or an explicit workflow and optionally the project path and original request for context. Focus areas are security, quality, performance, and comprehensive. Explicit workflows are pre-commit, pre-merge, and quality-audit.

focus.description: Focus area for smart workflow selection (optional)

prompt.description: Original user request for workflow context (optional)

cards.name: run_workflow
usage_rules: Use this tool when the user asks to review their code, check their code, or analyze something.
For an ambiguous request, omit workflow and focus so the tool can seek clarification.
For a request that specifies an area, provide the matching focus; for a request that names a direct workflow, provide workflow instead.
When the request includes useful intent or context, pass it in prompt so the workflow can use the original request.
Set projectPath to the project root when needed; if omitted, it defaults to the current working directory.
Only use the supported focus values: security, quality, performance, comprehensive.
Only use the supported workflow values: pre-commit, pre-merge, quality-audit.

cards.description: Retrieves the full content and metadata for one LeetCode community solution, including article text, author information, and navigation links.

topicId.description: The unique topic ID of the solution to retrieve. This ID can be obtained from the 'topicId' field in the response of the 'list_problem_solutions' tool. Format is typically a string of numbers and letters that uniquely identifies the solution in LeetCode's database.

cards.name: get_problem_solution
usage_rules: Provide the required topicId as a string; obtain it from a result returned by list_problem_solutions.
Use this to fetch a solution's full content after finding it in the solution list.

cards.description: Retrieves a LeetCode user's contest ranking, participation history, and contest performance information.

attended.description: Whether to include only the contests the user has participated in (true) or all contests (false); defaults to true

username.description: LeetCode username to retrieve contest ranking information for

cards.name: get_user_contest_ranking
usage_rules: Provide the required LeetCode username as a string.
attended is optional and defaults to true, which limits results to contests the user participated in; set it to false to include all contests.

cards.description: Retrieves a user's recent accepted submissions on LeetCode Global.

limit.description: Maximum number of accepted submissions to return (optional, defaults to server-defined limit)

username.description: LeetCode username to retrieve recent accepted submissions for

cards.name: get_recent_ac_submissions
usage_rules: Provide the required LeetCode username as a string.
Optionally set limit to control the maximum number of accepted submissions returned; its schema default is 10.

cards.description: Lists community solutions for a LeetCode problem, returning solution metadata such as topicId. Use get_problem_solution with a returned topicId to retrieve a solution's full content.

limit.description: Maximum number of solutions to return per request. Used for pagination and controlling response size. Default is 20 if not specified. Must be a positive integer.

orderBy.description: Sorting criteria for the returned solutions. 'DEFAULT' sorts by LeetCode's default algorithm (typically a combination of recency and popularity), 'MOST_VOTES' sorts by the number of upvotes (highest first), and 'MOST_RECENT' sorts by publication date (newest first).

questionSlug.description: The URL slug/identifier of the problem to retrieve solutions for (e.g., 'two-sum', 'add-two-numbers'). This is the same string that appears in the LeetCode problem URL after '/problems/'

skip.description: Number of solutions to skip before starting to collect results. Used in conjunction with 'limit' for implementing pagination. Default is 0 if not specified. Must be a non-negative integer.

tagSlugs.description: Array of tag identifiers to filter solutions by programming languages (e.g., 'python', 'java') or problem algorithm/data-structure tags (e.g., 'dynamic-programming', 'recursion'). Only solutions tagged with at least one of the specified tags will be returned.

userInput.description: Search term to filter solutions by title, content, or author name. Case insensitive. Useful for finding specific approaches or algorithms mentioned in solutions.

cards.name: list_problem_solutions
usage_rules: Provide the required questionSlug, the problem's URL slug (for example, two-sum).
Optionally set limit and skip to control the page size and pagination; the schema defaults limit to 10 and skip is not specified.
Optionally filter with tagSlugs and userInput. tagSlugs is an array of strings; userInput searches solution title, content, or author according to the tool description.
orderBy is optional and defaults to HOT. The schema lists HOT, MOST_VOTES, and the literal value " MOST_RECENT" (including its leading space); use the exact enum value accepted by the schema.
The limit description calls for a positive integer, and the skip description calls for a non-negative integer.

cards.description: Retrieves a user's recent LeetCode Global submissions, including accepted and failed submissions with metadata.

limit.description: Maximum number of submissions to return (optional, defaults to server-defined limit)

username.description: LeetCode username to retrieve recent submissions for

cards.name: get_recent_submissions
usage_rules: Provide the required LeetCode username as a string.
Optionally set limit to control the maximum number of submissions returned; its schema default is 10.

cards.description: Retrieves the current LeetCode Daily Challenge with problem details, including its description, constraints, and examples.
cards.name: get_daily_challenge
usage_rules: This tool takes no input properties; call it with an empty object.

cards.description: Searches LeetCode problems using category, difficulty, tags, and title or description keywords, with pagination controls.

category.description: Problem category filter (e.g., 'algorithms', 'database', 'shell') to narrow down the problem domain

difficulty.description: Problem difficulty level filter to show only problems of a specific difficulty

limit.description: Maximum number of problems to return in a single request (for pagination)

offset.description: Number of problems to skip (for pagination)

searchKeywords.description: Keywords to search in problem titles and descriptions

tags.description: List of topic tags to filter problems by (e.g., ['array', 'dynamic-programming', 'tree'])

cards.name: search_problems
usage_rules: All inputs are optional. category must be one of the schema's listed categories and defaults to all-code-essentials; difficulty, if provided, must be EASY, MEDIUM, or HARD.
searchKeywords supplies terms to search in problem titles and descriptions.
tags, if provided, must be an array of strings selected from the schema's listed tag values.
Use limit and offset for pagination; limit defaults to 10.

cards.description: Retrieves graduated hints for a LeetCode problem to offer progressive guidance without providing the complete solution.

titleSlug.description: The URL slug/identifier of the problem (e.g., 'two-sum', 'add-two-numbers') to retrieve hints for

cards.name: get_problem_hints
usage_rules: Provide the required titleSlug as a string, using the problem's URL slug (for example, two-sum).

cards.description: Retrieves comprehensive details for a LeetCode problem, including its description, examples, constraints, test cases, and related information.

titleSlug.description: The URL slug/identifier of the problem (e.g., 'two-sum', 'add-two-numbers') as it appears in the LeetCode URL

cards.name: get_problem
usage_rules: Provide the required titleSlug as a string, using the problem's URL slug (for example, two-sum).

cards.description: Retrieves a LeetCode user's profile information, statistics, solved-problem information, and profile details.

username.description: LeetCode username to retrieve profile information for

cards.name: get_user_profile
usage_rules: Provide the required LeetCode username as a string.

cards.description: Applies LikeC4’s semantic layout to a saved view, identified by view ID. Uses the default project unless another project ID is supplied.

projectId.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

viewId.description: View ID to apply semantic layout to

cards.name: apply-semantic-layout
usage_rules: Provide the required viewId.
Optionally provide projectId; it defaults to "default".

cards.description: Renders a saved LikeC4 view as an interactive diagram in chat, with pan, zoom, and fit controls. Use this when the user wants to see a view; use read-view when they only need its structure.

fullModel.description: Include the complete model instead of data scoped to this view

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

fitView.description: Fit the diagram into the canvas initially

cards.name: render-view
usage_rules: Provide the required viewId and optionally the project (default: "default").
Set fullModel to true to include the complete model instead of data scoped to the view; it defaults to false.
The render options can set canvas size (compact, standard, or large), fitView (default: true), and initialZoom (0.05–3). initialZoom overrides fitView.

cards.description: Summarizes an element’s descendants in breadth-first order, reporting each descendant’s depth, tags, metadata, and child and relationship counts. Returns at most 200 descendants and reports truncation, including truncation by depth. This is more efficient than reading each descendant individually.

elementId.description: Parent element id (FQN) whose descendants to summarize

maxDepth.description: Maximum depth of descendants to include (default: 10, max: 20)

metadataKeys.description: If provided, only include these metadata keys in the response

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: subgraph-summary
usage_rules: Provide the required elementId as a fully qualified element ID (FQN); project defaults to "default".
maxDepth defaults to 10 and must be from 1 to 20.
Optionally supply metadataKeys to restrict returned metadata to those keys.
The result is capped at 200 descendants; check its truncation indicators if a complete summary is needed.

cards.description: Finds elements and deployment nodes by exact tags using allOf (all listed tags), anyOf (at least one listed tag), and noneOf (no listed tags). Conditions supplied together are combined with AND. Returns at most 50 results.

allOf.description: Element must have ALL these tags (AND)

anyOf.description: Element must have ANY of these tags (OR)

noneOf.description: Element must have NONE of these tags (NOT)

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: query-by-tags
usage_rules: Supply at least one non-empty tag condition: allOf, anyOf, or noneOf.
Tags are case-sensitive; use query-by-tag-pattern for partial tag-name matching.
The project argument defaults to "default".
The result is limited to 50 matches.

cards.description: Previews a draft LikeC4 view DSL definition against an existing project’s real elements without saving it. Intended for iterating before creating a view.

fullModel.description: Include the complete model instead of data scoped to this view

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: preview-view
usage_rules: Provide dsl containing a single element view definition in the form view <id> ... { ... }.
Use a new view ID: an existing ID is rejected. Use render-view to render an already-saved view.
Dynamic and deployment views are not supported and fail with a generic view-not-found error.
Custom theme and style extensions are not applied.
The project defaults to "default"; set fullModel to true to include the complete model rather than data scoped to the view (default: false).

cards.description: Lists the LikeC4 projects available in the workspace.
cards.name: list-projects
usage_rules: No arguments are required.
Use a listed project ID as the project argument when calling other tools that support project selection.

cards.description: Finds direct relationships between two elements and indirect relationships through their nested elements. Relationship details include kind, title, technology, tags, views in which they appear, and source location. Result order is not guaranteed.

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: find-relationships
usage_rules: Provide both element1 and element2 as fully qualified element IDs (FQNs); project defaults to "default".
Use find-relationship-paths for multi-hop relationship chains.

cards.description: Reads a single element in full, including properties, metadata, links, children, views containing it, direct and indirect incoming and outgoing relationships, deployed instances, and source location.

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: read-element
usage_rules: Provide the required id as a fully qualified element ID (FQN); project defaults to "default".
For multiple elements, use batch-read-elements instead.

cards.description: Reads one deployment node or deployed instance, including kind, tags, metadata, links, children, views containing it, source location, and—if it is a deployed instance—the element it instantiates. Children are empty for an instance.

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: read-deployment
usage_rules: Provide the required id as a fully qualified deployment ID (FQN); project defaults to "default".

cards.description: Traverses downstream dependencies from an element: returns elements that consume its output, directly or transitively, as a graph with each node’s depth and outgoers. Traversal stops at maxDepth or maxNodes and indicates when results are truncated.

elementId.description: Target element id (FQN) to query outgoers for

includeIndirect.description: Include indirect relationships through nested elements (default: true)

maxNodes.description: Maximum number of nodes to return (default: 200, max: 2000)

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: query-outgoers-graph
usage_rules: Provide the required elementId as a fully qualified element ID (FQN); project defaults to "default".
includeIndirect defaults to true and controls whether indirect relationships through nested elements are included.
maxDepth defaults to 10 and must be a positive integer no greater than 50; maxNodes defaults to 200 and must be a positive integer no greater than 2000.
If truncated is true, increase maxNodes or reduce maxDepth as appropriate.

cards.description: Compares two elements in the same project, showing differing properties, tags and metadata that are unique to either side or shared, and incoming and outgoing relationship counts for each side or shared.

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: element-diff
usage_rules: Provide element1Id and element2Id as fully qualified element IDs (FQNs) in the same project.
The project argument defaults to "default".

cards.description: Finds elements whose tags match a supplied pattern, returning matching tags per element and all distinct matching tags. Matching is case-insensitive and supports prefix, contains, or suffix modes.

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: query-by-tag-pattern
usage_rules: Provide a non-empty pattern; project defaults to "default".
matchMode accepts prefix, contains, or suffix and defaults to prefix.
At most 50 results are returned. For exact tag matching with boolean conditions, use query-by-tags.

cards.description: Search elements and deployment nodes across all projects by ID, title, kind, shape, tag, or metadata key. Returns the total match count and the first 20 results; use returned IDs with read tools.

search.description: Case-insensitive. "kind:<value>" or "shape:<value>" matches a kind or shape exactly, "meta:<key>" elements with that metadata key, "#<value>" tags containing the value; anything else matches id (FQN) or title.

cards.name: search-element
usage_rules: Provide a case-insensitive search string of at least 2 characters.
Use kind:<value> or shape:<value> to match a kind or shape exactly; use meta:<key> to find elements with a metadata key; use #<value> to find tags containing a value.
Any other search string is matched against element IDs (FQNs) or titles.

cards.description: Find relationship paths from one element to another, ordered shortest first, with up to 100 paths. By default, paths follow direct relationships only; optionally include implied relationships through nested elements.

includeIndirect.description: Include indirect (implied) relationships through nested elements (default: false)

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: find-relationship-paths
usage_rules: Provide sourceId and targetId as element FQNs; they must differ.
maxDepth defaults to 3 and must be between 1 and 5; includeIndirect defaults to false.
project defaults to "default". No connection returns an empty list.

cards.description: Find elements and deployment nodes with a specified metadata key and, optionally, a matching value. Returns at most 50 results.

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

value.description: Metadata value to match (ignored for exists mode)

cards.name: query-by-metadata
usage_rules: Provide the metadata key. project defaults to "default".
matchMode defaults to exact: it compares values case-sensitively. contains matches a substring case-insensitively; exists matches any item with the key and ignores value.
Provide value when using exact or contains; value is ignored for exists. For array metadata values, a match on any item qualifies.

cards.description: Read a view's structure, including its nodes, edges, and source location. Nodes may be elements, deployment nodes, or deployed instances. If the view has no title, its ID is used as the title.

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: read-view
usage_rules: Provide the viewId (view name); project defaults to "default".
Use render-view to show the diagram to the user.

cards.description: Read summaries for multiple elements in one call, including properties, metadata, children, relationship counts, views that include them, links, and source location. IDs not found are reported in notFound rather than failing the call.

ids.description: Array of element ids (FQNs) to read (max 50)

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: batch-read-elements
usage_rules: Provide 1–50 element IDs as FQNs; project defaults to "default".
Use read-element instead when you also need relationships, deployedInstances, defaultView, or project.

cards.description: Recursively traverse upstream relationships to return every element that feeds into a target, directly or transitively, as a graph with each node's depth and incomers.

elementId.description: Target element id (FQN) to query incomers for

includeIndirect.description: Include indirect relationships through nested elements (default: true)

maxNodes.description: Maximum number of nodes to return (default: 200, max: 2000)

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: query-incomers-graph
usage_rules: Provide the target element FQN as elementId; project defaults to "default".
includeIndirect defaults to true. maxDepth defaults to 10 and is limited to 1–50; maxNodes defaults to 200 and is limited to 1–2000.
Traversal stops at maxDepth or maxNodes. If truncated is true, increase maxNodes or lower maxDepth.

cards.description: Summarize a LikeC4 project: configuration, specification (element, relationship, and deployment kinds, tags, and metadata keys), and all elements, deployment entities, and views with their IDs, kinds, titles, and tags.

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: read-project-summary
usage_rules: Use this to orient yourself in a project before reading individual elements or views.
project defaults to "default".

cards.description: Run a one-step graph query around an element. Hierarchy queries return ancestors, descendants, siblings, children, or parent; relationship queries return single-hop incomers or outgoers. Results are limited to 100.

includeIndirect.description: For incomers/outgoers: include indirect relationships (default: true)

project.description: Project id (optional, will use "default" if not specified)

cards.name: query-graph
usage_rules: Provide elementId as an element FQN and choose queryType: ancestors, descendants, siblings, children, parent, incomers, or outgoers. project defaults to "default".
For incomers and outgoers, includeIndirect defaults to true and adds relationships of nested children. It is ignored for hierarchy queries.
Use query-incomers-graph or query-outgoers-graph for recursive relationship traversal.

cards.description: Tracks multiple independent approaches to a problem so they can be compared, revised, abandoned, or combined. Each call records a step for one path, its status, and whether the exploration is ready for synthesis.

needsNewPath.description: Whether to create a new parallel path

pathId.description: Identifier for the current reasoning path

readyForSynthesis.description: Whether ready to synthesize all paths

thought.description: Current thinking step within this path

thoughtInPath.description: Thought number within this specific path

totalPaths.description: Total number of paths being explored

cards.name: parallel-thinking
usage_rules: Use when comparing distinct strategies or perspectives in parallel; use sequentialthinking for a single evolving analysis path.
For every call, provide pathId, thought, pathNumber, totalPaths, thoughtInPath, pathStatus, and readyForSynthesis.
Use pathNumber and thoughtInPath values of at least 1; totalPaths must also be at least 1.
Set pathStatus to active, completed, abandoned, or merged. Use relatedPaths to identify relevant or conflicting path IDs when useful.
Use convergenceDetected and needsNewPath to report convergence or the need to open another approach when relevant.
Set readyForSynthesis to true only after the viable paths have been sufficiently explored.

cards.description: Supports flexible, sequential problem-solving in which each step can extend, revise, or branch from earlier analysis. Use it to develop and check one coherent line of analysis when the problem benefits from incremental progress or course correction.

nextThoughtNeeded.description: Whether another thought step is needed

totalThoughts.description: Estimated total thoughts needed (numeric value, e.g., 5, 10)

cards.name: sequentialthinking
usage_rules: Use for a single evolving analysis path; use parallel-thinking when developing multiple approaches simultaneously.
For every call, provide thought, nextThoughtNeeded, thoughtNumber, and totalThoughts. Both numeric fields must be integers of at least 1.
Adjust totalThoughts as the analysis evolves; thoughtNumber may exceed the initial estimate when more steps are needed.
When revising, set isRevision and identify the earlier step with revisesThought. When branching, use branchFromThought and, if useful, branchId.
Use needsMoreThoughts to indicate that additional analysis is needed when nearing an apparent endpoint.
Set nextThoughtNeeded to false only when the analysis is complete and a satisfactory result is ready.

cards.description: Export the current diagram to the required file path. The file extension can determine the format; an explicit format can also be supplied.
cards.name: export_diagram
usage_rules: Provide path; it is the only required argument.
Use format only when needed; accepted values are drawio, png, and svg.
Ensure the path has an extension compatible with the desired export format when relying on extension-based detection.

cards.description: Start a diagram session with an embedded server and open draw.io in a browser for a real-time preview of diagram updates.
cards.name: start_session
usage_rules: Call with no arguments; the input object has no properties.

cards.description: Fetch and return the current diagram XML from the browser, including manual edits made there. Use it to inspect the latest diagram state and its cell IDs before editing existing elements.
cards.name: get_diagram
usage_rules: Call with no arguments; the input object has no properties.
Call before edit_diagram when updating or deleting existing elements so operations use the current cell IDs and structure.

cards.description: Apply ID-based add, update, or delete operations to cells in the current diagram. Added or updated cells require complete mxCell XML, including mxGeometry; deletion requires only the cell ID.
cards.name: edit_diagram
usage_rules: Call get_diagram first to fetch the latest browser state, including manual edits, and inspect the cell IDs and structure.
Provide operations as an array; each operation must include operation and cell_id.
Use only update, add, or delete as the operation value.
For add and update, provide new_xml containing the complete mxCell element, including mxGeometry; choose a unique ID for an added cell.
For delete, provide the existing cell_id; new_xml is not needed.
Use update to replace an existing cell, add to create a cell, and delete to remove one.

cards.description: Create a new diagram from full mxGraphModel XML, replacing the current diagram. Use this for a diagram from scratch or a complete redesign; use edit_diagram for smaller changes to existing cells.
cards.name: create_new_diagram
usage_rules: Always provide the required xml argument containing a full mxGraphModel structure.
Include the root and its mxCell elements in the XML; IDs 0 and 1 are reserved, and top-level shapes should use parent="1".
Use edit_diagram instead for small changes such as adding or removing individual elements or changing labels, colors, or positions.
Keep the layout within the stated single-page viewport guidance (x=0–800, y=0–600) and follow the supplied spacing and edge-routing guidance when applicable.

cards.description: Returns task recommendations based on project status, dependencies, priorities, and optionally complexity. You can filter by project, favor tags, and limit the number of recommendations.

considerComplexity.description: Whether to factor in task complexity for recommendations

excludeBlocked.description: Whether to exclude blocked tasks from recommendations

maxRecommendations.description: Maximum number of task recommendations to return

preferredTags.description: Preferred task tags to prioritize in recommendations

projectId.description: Filter recommendations to a specific project

workingDirectory.description: The full absolute path to the working directory where data is stored. MUST be an absolute path, never relative. Windows: "C:\Users\username\project" or "D:\projects\my-app". Unix/Linux/macOS: "/home/username/project" or "/Users/username/project". Do NOT use: ".", "..", "~", "./folder", "../folder" or any relative paths. Ensure the path exists and is accessible before calling this tool. NOTE: When server is started with --claude flag, this parameter is ignored and a global user directory is used instead.

cards.name: get_next_task_recommendation
usage_rules: Provide workingDirectory as an existing, accessible absolute path; relative paths are not valid. When the server runs with --claude, this parameter is ignored in favor of a global user directory.
Use projectId to restrict recommendations to one project; preferredTags to prioritize matching tags.
maxRecommendations must be from 1 to 10. considerComplexity and excludeBlocked control whether complexity is considered and blocked tasks are excluded; both default to true.

cards.description: Deletes the task identified by id. The required confirmation flag is a safeguard against accidental deletion.

confirm.description: Must be set to true to confirm deletion (safety measure)

id.description: The unique identifier of the task to delete

workingDirectory.description: The full absolute path to the working directory where data is stored. MUST be an absolute path, never relative. Windows: "C:\Users\username\project" or "D:\projects\my-app". Unix/Linux/macOS: "/home/username/project" or "/Users/username/project". Do NOT use: ".", "..", "~", "./folder", "../folder" or any relative paths. Ensure the path exists and is accessible before calling this tool. NOTE: When server is started with --claude flag, this parameter is ignored and a global user directory is used instead.

cards.name: delete_task
usage_rules: Provide workingDirectory as an existing, accessible absolute path; relative paths are not valid. When the server runs with --claude, this parameter is ignored in favor of a global user directory.
Provide the task's unique id and set confirm to true to authorize deletion.

cards.description: Retrieves a subtask by its unique id, including its available details and parent-task context.

id.description: The unique identifier of the subtask to retrieve

workingDirectory.description: The full absolute path to the working directory where data is stored. MUST be an absolute path, never relative. There are usually two scenarios: one is to simply display the regional composition, only `fillColor` needs to be configured, and all administrative divisions are consistent, representing that all blocks are connected as one; the other is the regional data distribution scenario, first determine the `dataType`, `dataValueUnit` and `dataLabel` configurations, `dataValue` should be a meaningful value and consistent with the meaning of dataType, and then determine the style configuration. The `fillColor` configuration represents the default fill color for areas without data. Lower-level administrative divisions do not need `fillColor` configuration, and their fill colors are determined by the `colors` configuration (If `dataType` is "number", only one base color (warm color) is needed in the list to calculate the continuous data mapping color band; if `dataType` is "enum", the number of color values in the list is equal to the number of enumeration values (contrast colors)). If `subdistricts` has a value, `showAllSubdistricts` must be set to true. For example, {"title": "陕西省地级市分布图", "data": {"name": "陕西省", "showAllSubdistricts": true, "dataLabel": "城市", "dataType": "enum", "colors": ["#4ECDC4", "#A5D8FF"], "subdistricts": [{"name": "西安市", "dataValue": "省会"}, {"name": "宝鸡市", "dataValue": "地级市"}, {"name": "咸阳市", "dataValue": "地级市"}, {"name": "铜川市", "dataValue": "地级市"}, {"name": "渭南市", "dataValue": "地级市"}, {"name": "延安市", "dataValue": "地级市"}, {"name": "榆林市", "dataValue": "地级市"}, {"name": "汉中市", "dataValue": "地级市"}, {"name": "安康市", "dataValue": "地级市"}, {"name": "商洛市", "dataValue": "地级市"}]}, "width": 1000, "height": 1000}.

colors.description: Data color list, in rgb or rgba format.

dataType.description: The type of the data value, numeric or enumeration type

dataValue.description: Data value, numeric string or enumeration string.

name.description: Keywords for the Chinese name of an administrative region (must be within China), and must be one of China, province, city, district, or county. The name should be more specific and add attributive descriptions, for example, "西安市" is better than "西安", "杭州西湖区" is better than "西湖区". It cannot be a specific place name or a vague name, such as "其它".

style.description: Style settings.

fillColor.description: Fill color, rgb or rgba format.

subdistricts.description: Sub-administrative regions are used to display the regional composition or regional distribution of related data.

dataValue.description: Data value, numeric string or enumeration string.

name.description: Keywords for the Chinese name of an administrative region (must be within China), and must be one of China, province, city, district, or county. The name should be more specific and add attributive descriptions, for example, "西安市" is better than "西安", "杭州西湖区" is better than "西湖区". It cannot be a specific place name or a vague name, such as "其它".

style.description: Style settings.

fillColor.description: Fill color, rgb or rgba format.

height.description: Set the height of map, default is 1000.

title.description: The map title should not exceed 16 characters. The content should be consistent with the information the map wants to convey and should be accurate, rich, creative, and attractive.

width.description: Set the width of map, default is 1600.

cards.name: generate_district_map
usage_rules: Provide `title` and `data`; `data.name` must identify a specific Chinese administrative region (China, province, city, district, or county), not a specific place or vague label.

For a composition map, configure `style.fillColor`. For data distribution, supply `dataType` (`number` or `enum`) and meaningful `dataValue` values; use `dataLabel` and `dataValueUnit` as appropriate.
For subregion data, provide `subdistricts` with each region's `name` and, where applicable, `dataValue`; set `showAllSubdistricts` to true whenever `subdistricts` is provided.
Use `colors` for subregion data coloring: numeric data uses one base color for a continuous scale; enum data uses a color per category. `style.fillColor` is the default for areas without data.

cards.description: Creates a dual-axes combination chart, typically combining columns and lines to compare quantities and trends on different scales.

axisXTitle.description: Set the x-axis title of chart.

categories.description: Categories for dual axes chart, such as, ['2015', '2016', '2017'].

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

series.description: Series for dual axes chart, such as, [{ type: 'column', data: [91.9, 99.1, 101.6, 114.4, 121], axisYTitle: '销售额' }, { type: 'line', data: [0.055, 0.06, 0.062, 0.07, 0.075], 'axisYTitle': '利润率' }].

axisYTitle.description: Set the y-axis title of the chart series, such as, axisYTitle: '销售额'.

data.description: When type is column, the data represents quantities, such as [91.9, 99.1, 101.6, 114.4, 121]. When type is line, the data represents ratios and its values are recommended to be less than 1, such as [0.055, 0.06, 0.062, 0.07, 0.075].

type.description: The optional value can be 'column' or 'line'.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_dual_axes_chart
usage_rules: Provide a non-empty `categories` array and a non-empty `series` array. Each series requires `type` (`column` or `line`) and numeric `data`; provide one value per category for each series.
Use each series' optional `axisYTitle` to label its y-axis. Line-series data often represents ratios; values below 1 are recommended for ratios.
Optional settings include the x-axis title, chart dimensions, title, theme, and style.

cards.description: Creates a scatter chart for exploring relationships, trends, or distribution patterns between two numeric variables.

axisXTitle.description: Set the x-axis title of chart.

axisYTitle.description: Set the y-axis title of chart.

data.description: Data for scatter chart, such as, [{ x: 10, y: 15 }].

group.description: Group name for the data point.

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_scatter_chart
usage_rules: Provide a non-empty `data` array; every point must have numeric `x` and `y` values. An optional string `group` can identify a point's group.
Optional settings include axis titles, chart dimensions, title, theme, and style.

cards.description: Creates a word cloud that represents word frequency or weight through differences in text size.

data.description: Data for word cloud chart, it should be an array of objects, each object contains a `text` field and a `value` field, such as, [{ value: 4.272, text: '形成' }].

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_word_cloud_chart
usage_rules: Provide a non-empty `data` array of objects, each with a string `text` and numeric `value`.
Optional settings include chart dimensions, title, theme, and style.

cards.description: Creates a pie chart to show how a whole is divided among categories; set an inner radius to make it a donut chart.

data.description: Data for pie chart, it should be an array of objects, each object contains a `category` field and a `value` field, such as, [{ category: '分类一', value: 27 }].

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

innerRadius.description: Set the innerRadius of pie chart, the value between 0 and 1. Set the pie chart as a donut chart. Set the value to 0.6 or number in [0 ,1] to enable it.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_pie_chart
usage_rules: Provide a non-empty `data` array of objects with a string `category` and numeric `value`.
`innerRadius` defaults to 0; set it to a value from 0 to 1 to configure the central opening, for example 0.6 for a donut-style chart.
Optional settings include chart dimensions, title, theme, and style.

cards.description: Creates a flow diagram showing process or system steps and their connections.

data.description: Data for flow diagram chart, such as, { nodes: [{ name: 'node1' }, { name: 'node2' }], edges: [{ source: 'node1', target: 'node2', name: 'edge1' }] }.

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_flow_diagram
usage_rules: Provide `data` with both `nodes` and `edges`; `nodes` must contain at least one object with a `name`, and each edge requires string `source` and `target` values.
Use node names as the endpoint identifiers in edges. An edge may include an optional `name`.
Optional settings include chart dimensions, theme, and texture style.

cards.description: Creates an organization chart representing a hierarchy of people, roles, or units.

data.description: Data for organization chart which is a hierarchical structure, such as, { name: 'CEO', description: 'Chief Executive Officer', children: [{ name: 'CTO', description: 'Chief Technology Officer', children: [{ name: 'Dev Manager', description: 'Development Manager' }] }] }, and the maximum depth is 3.

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

orient.description: Orientation of the organization chart, either horizontal or vertical. Default is vertical, when the level of the chart is more than 3, it is recommended to use horizontal orientation.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_organization_chart
usage_rules: Provide `data` as a hierarchy of objects, each with a required `name`; `description` and nested `children` are optional.
The supported hierarchy has a maximum depth of 3. Choose `orient` as `horizontal` or `vertical`; it defaults to vertical, while horizontal is recommended for charts with more than 3 levels.
Optional settings include chart dimensions, theme, and texture style.

cards.description: Creates a violin chart to compare the distributions of numeric data across categories, optionally subdivided by groups.

axisXTitle.description: Set the x-axis title of chart.

axisYTitle.description: Set the y-axis title of chart.

data.description: Data for violin chart, such as, [{ category: '分类一', value: 10 }] or [{ category: '分类二', value: 20, group: '组别一' }].

category.description: Category of the data point, such as '分类一'.

group.description: Optional group for the data point, used for grouping in the violin chart.

value.description: Value of the data point, such as 10.

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_violin_chart
usage_rules: Provide a non-empty `data` array of objects with a string `category` and numeric `value`. An optional string `group` identifies a group for the data point.
Optional settings include axis titles, chart dimensions, title, theme, and style.

cards.description: Creates a line chart to show changes or trends across time or another ordered sequence.

axisXTitle.description: Set the x-axis title of chart.

axisYTitle.description: Set the y-axis title of chart.

data.description: Data for line chart, it should be an array of objects, each object contains a `time` field and a `value` field, such as, [{ time: '2015', value: 23 }, { time: '2016', value: 32 }].

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

lineWidth.description: Line width for the lines of chart, such as 4.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_line_chart
usage_rules: Provide a non-empty `data` array of objects with a string `time` and numeric `value`. An optional string `group` can distinguish multiple series.
Optional settings include axis titles, chart dimensions, title, theme, and style; style can set line width, palette, background color, and texture.

cards.description: Creates a Venn diagram to visualize overlaps and relationships among sets.

data.description: Data for venn chart, such as, [{ label: 'A', value: 10, sets: ['A'] }, { label: 'B', value: 20, sets: ['B'] }, { label: 'C', value: 30, sets: ['C'] }, { label: 'AB', value: 5, sets: ['A', 'B'] }].

label.description: Label for the venn chart segment, such as 'A', 'B', or 'C'.

sets.description: Array of set names that this segment belongs to, such as ['A', 'B'] for an intersection between sets A and B.

value.description: Value for the venn chart segment, such as 10, 20, or 30.

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_venn_chart
usage_rules: Provide a non-empty `data` array of objects with numeric `value` and a `sets` array of set names; `label` is optional.
Use `sets` to specify the set or combination of sets represented by each segment, such as `["A", "B"]` for an intersection.
Optional settings include chart dimensions, title, theme, and style.

cards.description: Generate a liquid chart that visualizes one value as a proportion, such as occupancy or project completion. Supports circle, rectangle, pin, and triangle shapes.

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

percent.description: The percentage value to display in the liquid chart, should be a number between 0 and 1, where 1 represents 100%. For example, 0.75 represents 75%.

shape.description: The shape of the liquid chart, can be 'circle', 'rect', 'pin', or 'triangle'. Default is 'circle'.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

color.description: Custom color for the liquid chart, if not specified, defaults to the theme color.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_liquid_chart
usage_rules: Provide the required percent as a number from 0 to 1 inclusive; for example, 0.75 represents 75%.
Optional width and height are numbers and default to 600 and 400. The title defaults to an empty string.
Shape may be circle, rect, pin, or triangle and defaults to circle. Theme may be default, academy, or dark and defaults to default.
Optional style can set backgroundColor, a custom liquid color, and texture (default or rough). Texture defaults to default.

cards.description: Generate a boxplot chart for summarizing and comparing distributions across categories, optionally separated into groups.

axisXTitle.description: Set the x-axis title of chart.

axisYTitle.description: Set the y-axis title of chart.

data.description: Data for boxplot chart, such as, [{ category: '分类一', value: 10 }] or [{ category: '分类二', value: 20, group: '组别一' }].

category.description: Category of the data point, such as '分类一'.

group.description: Optional group for the data point, used for grouping in the boxplot.

value.description: Value of the data point, such as 10.

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_boxplot_chart
usage_rules: Provide the required data as a non-empty array of objects. Each object must include a string category and numeric value; group is an optional string for grouping data.
Optional axisXTitle, axisYTitle, and title default to empty strings. Width and height default to 600 and 400.
Theme may be default, academy, or dark and defaults to default.
Optional style can set backgroundColor, a string-array palette, and texture (default or rough); texture defaults to default.

cards.description: Generate a radar chart for comparing multidimensional data, such as several products across criteria. Data points can be assigned to groups.

data.description: Data for radar chart, it should be an array of objects, each object contains a `name` field and a `value` field, such as, [{ name: 'Design', value: 70 }].

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

lineWidth.description: Line width for the lines of chart, such as 4.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_radar_chart
usage_rules: Provide the required data as a non-empty array of objects. Each object must have a string name and numeric value; group is an optional string.
For a meaningful multidimensional comparison, use data points representing the dimensions being compared; use group to distinguish series when needed.
Optional title defaults to an empty string; width and height default to 600 and 400.
Theme may be default, academy, or dark and defaults to default. Optional style can set backgroundColor, lineWidth, a string-array palette, and texture (default or rough); texture defaults to default.

cards.description: Generate a table chart that presents structured data in rows and columns, suitable for detailed information and precise values.

data.description: Data for table chart, such as, [{ "Name": "胡彦斌", "Age": 32, "Address": "西湖区湖底公园1号" }, { "Name": "吴彦祖", "Age": 42, "Address": "西湖区湖底公园1号" }]. Each item in the array represents a row, and the keys of each item represent the column names.

height.description: Set the height of chart, default is 400.

style.description: Style configuration for the chart with a JSON object, optional.

backgroundColor.description: Background color of the chart, such as, '#fff'.

palette.description: Color palette for the chart, it is a collection of colors.

texture.description: Set the texture for the chart, optional, default is 'default'. 'rough' refers to hand-drawn style.

theme.description: Set the theme for the chart, optional, default is 'default'.

width.description: Set the width of chart, default is 600.

cards.name: generate_table
usage_rules: Provide the required data as a non-empty array of objects. Each object represents a row, and its keys provide the column names; row objects may contain additional properties.
Optional title defaults to an empty string; width and height default to 600 and 400.
Theme may be default, academy, or dark and defaults to default. Optional style can set backgroundColor, a string-array palette, and texture (default or rough); texture defaults to default.

cards.description: Retrieve metadata for a file or directory within the allowed directories. Results can include size, timestamps, permissions, type, and text-file line positions; Excel files may include sheet dimensions.
cards.name: get_file_info
usage_rules: Provide the target as path; absolute paths are most reliable.
Use this to inspect metadata rather than read file contents.

cards.description: Read output from a running process by PID, with pagination and process-state detection.
cards.name: read_process_output
usage_rules: Supply the process PID. offset=0 reads new output since the previous read and may wait up to timeout_ms; a positive offset reads from an absolute line position, and a negative offset reads from the end.
Use length to cap the number of lines; output is subject to the configured fileReadLineLimit.
Use the returned state to determine whether the process is waiting for input, finished, or still running.

cards.description: Set a configuration value by key. Configuration changes can affect subsequent file and command behavior.
cards.name: set_config_value
usage_rules: Provide key and value; origin is optional and must be ui or llm when supplied.
Use a value type appropriate to the setting, such as an array of strings for allowedDirectories or a boolean for telemetryEnabled.
Treat configuration as trusted input. Setting allowedDirectories to an empty array permits access to the entire filesystem.

cards.description: Read a local file or, when isUrl is true, fetch content from a URL. Supports line-based pagination for text, structured extraction for common document formats, and content retrieval for images.
cards.name: read_file
usage_rules: Provide path. Local files must be within allowed directories; absolute paths are most reliable.

For text, offset is a zero-based line position and length limits returned lines. Negative offset reads from the end; length is ignored for negative offsets. URL content is read in full regardless of pagination.
For Excel files, optionally select sheet by name or zero-based index as a string and use range in FROM:TO form; offset and length can paginate rows as a fallback. For PDFs, pagination is by page.
DOCX reads return a text-bearing outline by default. A nonzero offset with length requests paginated raw XML; offset=0 returns the outline.
Set isUrl=true to read a URL rather than a local path.

cards.description: Start a background search of a directory for matching file names or file contents. Returns a session identifier for retrieving progressive results or stopping the search.
cards.name: start_search
usage_rules: Provide path and pattern. Choose searchType=files for file-name patterns and searchType=content for text inside files; the default is files.
Patterns are regular expressions by default. Set literalSearch=true for exact-string matching, especially when the pattern contains regex metacharacters.
Use filePattern to filter searched files, ignoreCase for case sensitivity, includeHidden to include hidden entries, and contextLines to control surrounding content lines.
Use the returned search session with the available result-retrieval or stop-search tools. Ambiguous requests may benefit from separate file-name and content searches.

cards.description: List active background searches, including their identifiers, types, patterns, statuses, and runtimes.
cards.name: list_searches
usage_rules: Call without parameters to inspect active searches.

cards.description: Write content to a file, replacing it by default or appending when requested. Supports text and spreadsheet data; use the dedicated PDF tool to create or modify PDFs.
cards.name: write_file
usage_rules: Provide path and content. Files must be within allowed directories; absolute paths are most reliable.
The default mode is rewrite, which replaces the file contents. Set mode=append to add content to the end.
Excel content may be a JSON 2D array or an object mapping sheet names to 2D arrays.
For long content, multiple calls can use rewrite followed by append; inspect the file if a prior write was partial.

cards.description: Forcefully terminate a running process by PID.
cards.name: kill_process
usage_rules: Provide the process PID and verify it is the intended process before terminating; termination is forceful.

cards.description: List active terminal sessions with process identifiers, blocked status, and runtime.
cards.name: list_sessions
usage_rules: Call without parameters to inspect sessions. A blocked session may be waiting for input, as with a REPL.

cards.description: Gracefully stop an active background search. Its final results remain available until cleanup, typically after five minutes.
cards.name: stop_search
usage_rules: Provide the search sessionId. Use this when the search is no longer needed or is taking too long.

cards.description: Create a PDF from Markdown or modify an existing PDF with page insertions and deletions. Supports Markdown, HTML/CSS, SVG, and images when creating PDF content.
cards.name: write_pdf
usage_rules: Provide path and content. For creation, content is a Markdown string; for modifications, content is an array of insert or delete operations using zero-based page indexes.
When modifying an existing PDF, write the result to a different outputPath to preserve the original. Creating a PDF requires an output path for the new file.
A delete operation requires pageIndexes. An insert operation requires pageIndex and may include markdown or sourcePdfPath.
Use a page-break HTML element in Markdown to force a page break. Files must be within allowed directories.

cards.description: Return summary statistics about tool usage, including success and failure rates and performance metrics.
cards.name: get_usage_stats
usage_rules: Call without parameters to retrieve usage statistics.

cards.description: Opens the Desktop Commander feedback form in a browser. The form collects survey answers; this tool does not accept or prefill them. It automatically includes usage metadata such as command count, days of use, platform, and client ID.
cards.name: give_feedback_to_desktop_commander
usage_rules: Call with an empty object; no input parameters are required.
Do not provide survey answers as tool arguments.

cards.description: Returns recent local tool-call history, including arguments and outputs, in chronological order. Useful for recovering context or debugging calls. History is stored locally, retains up to 1,000 calls in memory, and replaces outputs over 4 KiB with an omission marker. This tool does not record its own calls or calls to track_ui_event.
cards.name: get_recent_tool_calls
usage_rules: Optionally set maxResults (default 50; minimum 1, maximum 1,000), since (a date-time), or toolName to filter results.
Do not expect this call or track_ui_event calls to appear in the returned history.

cards.description: Starts a terminal process on the authorized macOS device and detects whether it is waiting for input, has completed, or is still running. Suitable for shell commands, interactive REPLs, scripts, and long-running work. The default shell is /bin/zsh; a running process can be followed up with interact_with_process or read_process_output.
cards.name: start_process
usage_rules: Provide both required arguments: command and timeout_ms. Optionally set shell, origin (ui or llm), and verbose_timing.
Use a suitable timeout_ms for the command; a still-running process can be followed up using its process ID.
Absolute paths are most reliable; relative paths depend on the working directory, and tilde paths may not resolve in every context.
On macOS, Python may be invoked as python3; Homebrew is commonly used, and system protections may block some operations.
Set verbose_timing to true when detailed timing and exit information is needed.

cards.description: Lists running processes and reports process information including PID, command name, CPU usage, and memory usage.
cards.name: list_processes
usage_rules: Call with an empty object; this tool has no input parameters.

cards.description: Sends text or a command to an existing terminal or REPL process and returns newly available output. It can wait for a recognized prompt, detect errors or completion, and report execution status.
cards.name: interact_with_process
usage_rules: Provide the required pid of the process and input to send; the PID is returned by start_process.
Optionally set timeout_ms, wait_for_prompt, or verbose_timing. The documented defaults are 8,000 ms, true, and false, respectively.
Use this for follow-up input to interactive or long-running processes; it does not start a process.

cards.description: Creates a directory, including any needed parent directories, or ensures that it exists. Access is limited to allowed directories.
cards.name: create_directory
usage_rules: Provide the required path.
Prefer an absolute path; relative paths depend on the current working directory, and tilde paths may not resolve in every context.
Only create directories within allowed directories.

cards.description: Returns a structured listing of files and directories under a specified path, optionally recursing to the requested depth. usage_rules: Provide the required path; optionally set depth (default 2) and origin (ui or llm).

Prefer an absolute path; relative paths depend on the current working directory, and tilde paths may not resolve in every context.
Expect nested directories with more than 100 items to be truncated in the listing.

cards.name: read_multiple_files
usage_rules: Provide paths as an array in the required paths argument.
Only read files within allowed directories.

Only edit files in allowed directories. Prefer absolute paths; relative paths depend on the current working directory, and tilde paths may not resolve in every context.

cards.description: Returns the complete Desktop Commander server configuration as JSON, including blocked commands, default shell, allowed directories, file read and write line limits, telemetry setting, connected-client information, version, and system information.
cards.name: get_config
usage_rules: Call with an empty object or optionally set origin to ui or llm.
Use the result to inspect configuration; this tool does not take configuration changes as input.

cards.description: Moves a file or directory to a destination, optionally renaming it as part of the move. Both source and destination must be within allowed directories.
cards.name: move_file
usage_rules: Provide both source and destination paths.
Prefer absolute paths because they do not depend on the current working directory.

cards.description: 根据公历或农历出生时间和性别获取八字信息。

lunarDatetime.description: 农历时间。例如农历2000年5月初五中午12点整表示为：`2000-5-5 12:00:00`。

cards.name: getBaziDetail
usage_rules: 必须提供 gender：0 表示女性，1 表示男性。

bazi.description: 八字，按年柱、月柱、日柱、时柱顺序，用空格隔开。例如：戊寅 己未 己卯 辛未

cards.name: getSolarTimes

cards.description: 获取指定公历日期时间的黄历信息；未提供时间时默认查询今天。
cards.name: getChineseCalendar
usage_rules: solarDatetime 为可选参数；如提供，使用带时区的 ISO 时间格式，例如 2008-03-01T13:00:00+08:00。

cards.description: Lists all variables currently defined in the math context.

usage_rules: Call with no arguments.

cards.name: validate_syntax

cards.description: Clears all variables defined in the math context.

cards.description: Retrieves the value associated with a variable in the math context.

cards.description: Evaluates a mathematical expression and stores its value under the specified variable name in the math context.

expression.description: Mathematical expression to evaluate and store

cards.description: Evaluates a mathematical expression using strict grammar validation, or checks its syntax without evaluating when requested.

cards.description: 将数值从一种速度单位换算为另一种，支持 mps、kmh、mph、fps 和 knot。
cards.name: speed_conversion
usage_rules: 提供数值以及 from_unit 和 to_unit；两个单位都必须是支持的单位代码。

cards.description: 根据实部和虚部计算复数的共轭。
cards.name: complex_conjugate
usage_rules: 必须同时提供 real 和 imag 两个数值。

cards.description: 将数值从一种时间单位换算为另一种，支持 ms、second、minute、hour、day、week、month 和 year。
cards.name: time_conversion
usage_rules: 提供数值以及 from_unit 和 to_unit；两个单位都必须是支持的单位代码。

cards.description: 将大于 1 的正整数分解为素因数的乘积。
cards.name: primeFactorization
usage_rules: n 必须是大于或等于 2 的整数。

cards.description: 计算输入值的反正切，结果以弧度表示。
cards.name: atan
usage_rules: 提供一个数值；输入不要求限制在特定区间内。

cards.description: 计算输入值的反正弦，结果以弧度表示。
cards.name: asin
usage_rules: 输入值应在 -1 到 1（含端点）之间。

cards.description: 计算从 n 个元素中选取 r 个元素的组合数 C(n,r)，不考虑顺序。
cards.name: combination
usage_rules: n 和 r 都必须是非负整数。
通常应满足 r ≤ n。

cards.description: 计算数字数组中所有元素的乘积。
cards.name: product
usage_rules: numbers 必须是由数值组成的数组。

cards.description: 计算 a 除以 b 的余数。
cards.name: modulo
usage_rules: 提供数值 a 和 b。
b 不应为 0。

cards.description: 逐元素计算 matrix_a 减去 matrix_b。
cards.name: matrix_subtract
usage_rules: 两个输入都应为二维数值数组。
两个矩阵应具有相同的行数和列数。

cards.description: 根据底面半径和高度计算圆锥体的体积与表面积。

height.description: 高度

cards.name: cone_calculation
usage_rules: radius 和 height 都必须是大于 0 的数值。

cards.description: 计算从 n 个元素中选取 r 个元素的排列数 P(n,r)，考虑顺序。
cards.name: permutation
usage_rules: n 和 r 都必须是非负整数。
通常应满足 r ≤ n。

cards.description: 计算数值 a 的立方根。
cards.name: cbrt
usage_rules: 必须提供数值参数 a。

cards.description: 计算输入方阵的逆矩阵。
cards.name: matrix_inverse
usage_rules: 必须提供 matrix 二维数组；其内容应为方阵，即每行长度相同且与行数相等。
矩阵必须可逆；奇异矩阵没有逆矩阵。
数组元素必须是数字。

cards.description: 计算 value 的以 10 为底的对数。
cards.name: log10

usage_rules: 必须提供数值参数 value 和 base。
value 必须大于 0；base 必须大于 0 且不等于 1。

cards.description: 计算 a 的 b 次幂。
cards.name: power
usage_rules: 必须提供数值参数 a（底数）和 b（指数）。
若要求实数结果，负底数不应搭配会产生非实数结果的指数。

cards.description: 根据半径和高度计算圆柱体的体积与表面积。

height.description: 高度

cards.name: cylinder_calculation
usage_rules: 必须提供数值参数 radius 和 height。
radius 与 height 均必须严格大于 0。

cards.description: 计算 value 的反双曲正切值。
cards.name: atanh
usage_rules: 必须提供数值参数 value。
为获得实数结果，value 必须严格位于 -1 与 1 之间；虽然输入模式未限制范围，端点处函数无有限实数值。

cards.description: 计算斐波那契数列从 0 开始编号的第 n 项。

cards.description: 生成斐波那契数列的前 n 项。
cards.name: fibonacciSequence
usage_rules: 必须提供整数 n，且 n 的范围为 1 到 100（含端点）。

cards.description: 将温度值从摄氏度、华氏度或开尔文转换为指定的目标温标。

cards.description: 找出数字数组中的最小值。

cards.description: 列出正整数 n 的所有因子。

usage_rules: 必须提供数值参数 value。

cards.description: 将两个复数相乘，并以实部和虚部输入复数分量。

cards.description: 判断输入的正整数是否为素数。
cards.name: isPrime

cards.description: 根据三条边的长度计算三角形的面积、周长等属性。

cards.description: 计算普通年金的现值，即按每期利率折现等额期末付款。

cards.name: tan
usage_rules: angle 必须以弧度提供。

cards.description: 计算二项式系数 C(n,k)，即从 n 个元素中选取 k 个元素的组合数。

cards.description: 将两个复数相加，并分别对实部和虚部进行加法运算。

cards.description: 计算以弧度表示的角度的余弦值。
cards.name: cos

cards.description: 将两个数值相加。
cards.name: add

cards.description: 计算二维数值矩阵的转置，即交换行和列。
